result.title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
result.comment: 49 pages, 8 figures. Work by Bowen Liu was done during an internship at Tencent Hy Team. Yuhan Li is Project Lead; Nuo Chen is corresponding author (chennuo26@gmail.com). Project page: https://acceleratebench.com/
result.summary: Application optimization requires coding agents to discover useful changes and coordinate them across a complete program while preserving the required computation. We introduce Accelerate Bench, a benchmark of 32 CPU optimization tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions. Each task provides a working program and specifies the workload, correctness requirements, timing boundaries, and permitted edits, leaving agents to choose where and how to optimize. Public testing supports iterative development, and a separate verifier scores the final submission. On benchmark version 1.1, we evaluate 16 coding agents, each pairing a model with a harness. Their Score@1 ranges from 25.5% to 67.4%. Most of their programs are correct, and the size of the speedup separates them: the two leading agents are at least 2x faster on 22 or more of the 32 tasks, while the other fourteen reach 2x on 8 to 17 and leave 125 of their 412 correct outcomes below 1.25x. Controlled replays show why coordination across an application matters: identical source code runs between 0.29x and 2.12x depending only on build and runtime settings, and one code change is worth 1.01x or 6.4x depending on another. Accelerate Bench pairs executable workloads with agents' programs and trajectories to evaluate both their gains and the process behind them.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 Accelerate Bench，包含 32 个来自科学应用与超算竞赛的 CPU 程序优化任务，用独立 verifier 对 16 个 coding agent 的加速比与正确性打分，并记录其程序与轨迹。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是应用级代码优化 agent 的执行速度与构建配置依赖，不涉及视觉证据、latent 推理状态或其使用；「单处改动价值随另一改动在 1.01x 与 6.4x 间变化」仅是表面类比于贡献分配，未提供可核查的状态、证据或训练线索。
